name: Teplizumab
route_note: IV infusion once daily for 14 consecutive days
originator: Jeffrey Bluestone and Kevan Herold (academic); MacroGenics, then Provention Bio

discovery.by: Jeffrey Bluestone, Kevan Herold and colleagues
discovery.note: A humanised, Fc-engineered (non-FcR-binding) version of the anti-CD3 antibody OKT3, designed to reduce cytokine release.

tagline: The first drug to delay the onset of type 1 diabetes
summary: Teplizumab is a humanised anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody given as a 14-day infusion course. In November 2022 it became the first therapy approved to delay the onset of clinical (stage 3) type 1 diabetes in people aged 8 and older who already have stage 2 disease, delaying diagnosis by about two years in the pivotal trial.
mechanism: Teplizumab binds the CD3ε component of the T-cell receptor complex. Its Fc region is mutated so it does not bind Fc receptors, reducing T-cell activation and cytokine release compared with the original OKT3.

Binding partially activates and modulates CD8+ T cells, leading to an 'exhausted' phenotype and expansion of regulatory-like cells, which slows the autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing beta cells.
uses: Delay of onset of stage 3 type 1 diabetes in adults and children aged 8 years and older with stage 2 type 1 diabetes

history.title: New-onset trial
history.detail: Herold and colleagues report that an anti-CD3 antibody preserves C-peptide in new-onset type 1 diabetes (NEJM 2002).

history.title: TN-10 prevention trial
history.detail: In relatives at high risk, teplizumab delays clinical type 1 diabetes by a median of about two years (NEJM 2019).

history.title: Complete response letter
history.detail: FDA declines approval pending pharmacokinetic comparability data.

history.title: PROTECT and Sanofi acquisition
history.detail: PROTECT shows preservation of beta-cell function in newly diagnosed patients; Sanofi acquires Provention Bio.

facts: Teplizumab is the first approved disease-modifying therapy for autoimmune type 1 diabetes.
Stage 2 type 1 diabetes is defined by two or more islet autoantibodies with abnormal glucose tolerance but no symptoms.

references.title: Herold KC et al. TN-10 teplizumab trial (NEJM 2019)
